sub.en: The passive moves the important thing to the front. Look at what each sentence is about.

items.q: The pillow ___ to help long-distance travellers.
items.why: The passive is be + past participle. Here the object of the action comes first.

items.q: It is a kind of hat that ___ over the head.
So far, over $195,000 ___ by its backers.
items.why: The passive works in every tense: has been + past participle for the present perfect.

items.q: More of them ___ in Portugal at the moment.
The run-down buildings ___ and turned into boutique hotels.

The gallery ___ from the main road.
items.why: After a modal the form is modal + be + past participle.

items.why: RECYCLED from Lesson 26: must for a deduction you are almost certain of.

acts.title: Active → passive, in four moves
steps: A studio in Madrid designed the pillow in 2012.
1 · Move the OBJECT to the front. It becomes the new subject.
2 · Put BE in the tense of the original verb: designed → was.
3 · Add the PAST PARTICIPLE of the main verb.
The pillow was designed by a studio in Madrid in 2012.
4 · Add BY + the old subject — only if it matters. Usually it does not.

items.q: Somebody stole the laptop. → The laptop ___.
They are renovating the warehouse. → The warehouse ___.
Backers have pledged the money. → The money ___.
You can see it from the road. → It ___ from the road.

lines: The pillow [was invented|invented|was inventing] to help long-distance travellers.

More of them [are being manufactured|are manufacturing|have manufactured] in Portugal at the moment.
The old warehouse [has been turned|has turned|is turning] into a gallery, and it [can be seen|can see|can been seen] from the main road.

items.why: The passive needs the past participle, not the past simple.
Leave out by + agent when it adds nothing. That is usually why the passive was chosen.

acts.title: The crowd will pay for it
text: Ali Ganjavian noticed something that anybody who travels a lot already knows: people fall asleep in the wrong places, badly. What he did about it was unusual. He designed a padded hat that is pulled over the head so that the wearer can take a nap almost anywhere, and then he did not go to a bank.

Twenty years ago the route was fixed. An idea was presented to a bank manager, a guarantee was asked for, a loan was granted or refused, and that was the end of the story. Nothing was manufactured until somebody with money had said yes.

Crowd-funding reversed the order. The idea is put on a website, a target is set, and anybody who likes it can pledge whatever they want. If the target is not reached, nobody is charged. Ganjavian’s pillow was funded this way: more than $195,000 was pledged by ordinary backers, most of whom simply wanted one. In the first three months of production, five thousand pillows were shipped to fifty-two countries.

The change is not only about money. Under the old system a product was tested after it had been made. Now it is tested before: if four thousand strangers will pay for something that does not exist yet, the market has answered the question that used to cost a fortune to ask.

It is not a guarantee of anything. Most campaigns fail, and a pledge is not a purchase — plenty of backers have paid for objects that were never delivered. But for anybody who is short of cash and has an idea that cannot easily be explained to a bank manager, the crowd is now the first place the question is asked.

items.s: The pillow is pulled over the head so that the wearer can sleep.
Ganjavian raised the money from a bank.
Under crowd-funding, backers are charged even if the target is not reached.
More than $195,000 was pledged for the pillow.
The text says the new system guarantees success.
Some backers have paid for things that were never delivered.

write.q: Describe how something around you is made, funded or run — a building, a product, a service, a local project. Use the passive at least five times, in at least three different tenses, and use by only where the agent actually matters.
plan: how it was made or funded
what is being done to it now
what can or cannot be done with it
write.model: The building I work in was put up in 1974 and was used as a printing works for almost thirty years. It was bought by a family from Astana in 2011 and has been divided into about twenty small offices since then. None of the renovation was funded by the city; the whole thing was paid for privately, which is why the corridors are still the original colour. Two more floors are being converted at the moment, and the lift is finally being replaced. The roof can be reached from the fourth floor, and in summer it is used by half the building for lunch. The parking, unfortunately, is still controlled by nobody at all.

speak.q: Describe a product you own, or a place you know, out loud. Say who or what made it, how it was paid for, and what is being done to it now. Use the passive.
